title: An attribute test whose quoted value is never closed hangs the compile forever
text_original:
* Fix inefficient attribute pattern

Found by @mauriceng98

* Fix lint
text_rewritten:
Same shape of failure as the unterminated bare value, but with quotes. If a caller sends an attribute test that opens a quoted value and never closes it -- a few hundred characters is enough, with either single or double quotes -- the compile never returns and the worker is gone. The input is plainly invalid, so it should come back as a syntax error in time proportional to its length.

Properly quoted values must keep working: values containing spaces, values containing the other quote character, values several hundred characters long, and the prefix/suffix/substring operators over quoted values.
body:
Same shape of failure as the unterminated bare value, but with quotes. If a caller sends an attribute test that opens a quoted value and never closes it -- a few hundred characters is enough, with either single or double quotes -- the compile never returns and the worker is gone. The input is plainly invalid, so it should come back as a syntax error in time proportional to its length.

acceptance_hint: An attribute test with an unterminated single- or double-quoted value raises a selector syntax error promptly however long the value is; properly quoted values are unchanged.
